## 2026-09-19 — Acquisition forecasts, evaluated retrieval and hosted-intelligence boundaries

### davidlarrimore/curatore-v2 — STRONG / MASTER REFERRAL — 29/30
- URL: https://github.com/davidlarrimore/curatore-v2
- Exact revision: `d4e42ac14450a58f84035c31db11b0399713a653`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Category: Repository / Public-data ETL / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: Functioning acquisition-forecast aggregation architecture spanning GSA Acquisition Gateway, DHS APFS and State Department forecast sources. The forecast layer normalizes buyer/agency, title/description, NAICS, PSC, set-aside, vehicle, estimated value, planned dates, POC/SBS and incumbent fields where available; preserves source-specific raw data; computes SHA-256 change hashes; retains `first_seen`/`last_updated`; stores field-level history; and records source-run status such as success, failed and partial.
- Rare / undernoticed value: It moves CaptureBrief earlier than the SAM opportunity stage. Planned-buy records and meaningful field changes can become auditable pre-solicitation pursuit signals instead of ad hoc analyst bookmarks, while degraded source runs stay distinguishable from legitimate no-change/no-record states.
- Buyer / painful problem: Federal BD/capture teams and proposal consultants want 6–18 month visibility into planned acquisitions but currently monitor multiple forecast portals with inconsistent fields and little change history.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Recurring forecast-to-pursuit radar for selected agencies: new/changed planned buys, field-change history, source health and later linkage to the eventual SAM notice when evidence supports continuity.
- Build-time / data advantage: Very high; roughly 3–6 months of connector, canonical forecast, history/change-detection and source-health design compressed into one working architecture.
- Evidence inspected: `docs/FORECAST_INTEGRATION.md`; `backend/app/api/v1/data/routers/forecasts.py`; `backend/app/connectors/gsa_gateway/ag_forecast_service.py`; exact current commit. The GSA service persists raw rows, computes change hashes and only snapshots meaningful field changes.
- Actual public license / rights: No repository-wide public license was found at the inspected revision. Per the user's standing assertion, repository-owned code/content is treated as separately commercially authorized. GSA/DHS/State forecast APIs/data and any hosted services remain separately governed and must be used under their own terms.
- Reuse classification: Working commercial-use assumption applies to repository-owned implementation. Forecast records are planning evidence, not commitments; never infer a future solicitation or incumbent transition without a later source-backed linkage.
- Score: A5 / B5 / C5 / D5 / E5 / F4 = **29/30**. F reflects external-source access/coverage boundaries, not the repository's missing public license under the user's standing authorization.
- Combination opportunities: Curatore forecast history -> official GSA Federal Hierarchy buyer normalization -> Sentinel/Market Map SAM packet once posted -> DATA Act/USAspending award lineage -> FAR/deviation evidence -> CaptureBrief pursuit packet.
- Next action: Benchmark 25 forecast records across the three supported sources, measure change-history/source-health fidelity and follow them forward to later SAM notices; require explicit `planning_only`, `linked`, `source_degraded` and `unresolved` states.

## 2026-09-19 — Award-ledger semantics and official buyer hierarchy

### Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/usaspend — STRONG / MASTER REFERRAL — 29/30
- URL: https://github.com/Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/usaspend
- Exact revision: `22aa2c936be4bc21764834bde24193aeb64934d4`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Category: Repository / Dataset Pipeline / Reusable Component
- Concrete capability: MIT R package that builds normalized organization × award × year panels from SAM UEIs plus USAspending transactions. The accounting layer treats awards as modification ledgers: dedupe, correction/deletion handling, action classification, deobligation netting, fiscal/calendar allocation, award-life identity, subaward direction and organization rollups are implemented and heavily tested.
- Rare / undernoticed value: It supplies accounting invariants that generic award APIs do not. Tests prove conservation under dedupe/corrections, support both as-posted and LIFO-restated deobligations, keep inbound subawards out of pass-through, distinguish internal/outbound/unrelated subawards, prevent multi-org double counting and mark parent-UEI-only matches `out_of_sample` instead of silently attributing them. That can make incumbent financial history materially more trustworthy.
- Buyer / painful problem: GovCon capture/market-intelligence teams and audit consultants need to understand an incumbent's actual award trajectory, modifications/deobligations and subaward behavior rather than summing transaction rows naively.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: 'Incumbent contract financial trajectory' section inside CaptureBrief: initial award, modification ledger, net obligation/deobligation history, award-life changes, subaward direction/coverage and disruption flags with explicit coverage state.
- Build-time / data advantage: Very high; several months of USAspending accounting/domain discovery, especially correction/delete semantics, award-family identifiers, subaward direction and fiscal/calendar conservation.
- Evidence inspected: `DESCRIPTION`; `R/accounting.R`, `R/reconcile.R`, `R/rollup.R`, `R/subsidiaries.R` and related source tree; `ACCOUNTING.md`; `tests/testthat/test-accounting.R`, including dedupe/reporting, correction/delete, LIFO deobligation, conservation, award-life/window-edge, subaward-direction, rollup and parent-UEI tests. The README contains a stale statement that the accounting layer is not implemented, but the inspected revision includes implementation and tests; source/test evidence controls this entry.
- Actual public license / rights: R package declares `MIT + file LICENSE`; the license file identifies the 2026 copyright holder. User's standing separate commercial authorization also applies to repository-owned code/content. USAspending/SAM/FSRS APIs/data and coverage remain separate federal-source concerns.
- Reuse classification: Reusable under MIT plus source-specific constraints. Accounting outputs must carry coverage and source-date metadata; never treat missing subaward coverage as zero pass-through.
- Score: A5 / B5 / C5 / D5 / E5 / F4 = **29/30**. F reflects external data/coverage semantics, not software-license uncertainty.
- Combination opportunities: Official DATA Act identity/PIID semantics -> usaspend modification ledger/accounting -> Big Local News FPDS disruption events -> CaptureBrief incumbent financial-history packet -> CivicProof/GovtIntel evidence gate.
- Next action: Build a 100-award golden set covering corrections, deobligations, parent/child entity identity, IDVs and subaward directions; compare naive summed obligations with the ledger-normalized result and quantify materially changed incumbent conclusions.
